rationale: Although the abstract briefly notes municipal water scarcity and unregulated private suppliers as regional background, the paper focuses on preserving peri-urban agricultural irrigation channel networks as nature-based blue infrastructure to enhance groundwater recharge and stormwater drainage/flood mitigation, and presents a policy/perspective argument rather than an empirical study or systematic review of household water or sanitation service access (E07).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Although the paper discusses planning, governance and policy frameworks for preserving blue infrastructure (satisfying broad institutional/policy language in the abstract), it is excluded under both readings because its core focus is irrigation channel networks for groundwater recharge and urban flood/stormwater drainage (E07) and it presents a conceptual policy argument rather than empirical water/sanitation service-access research.

evidence_quotes.quote: The potential contributions of irrigation channel networks to urban climate-resilience in the Hindu Kush Himalaya
We argue that, if maintained in urban environments, these channel networks would enhance groundwater recharge and facilitate drainage during storm events.
We discuss short- and long-term policies to enable this form of blue infrastructure to flourish, thereby supporting climate-resilient development
